neighbours.label: leaving a vehicle, mount or route: the particle or verb of getting off/out (dismount, pull off, get off, got out)
fire: When the bus reached the market, we got off and looked for a cafe.
The rider dismounted and led her horse across the stream.
If your tire goes flat, pull off onto the shoulder and turn on your lights.
He stepped out of the cab and paid the driver through the window.
Hikers can get off the trail at the second bridge to reach the village.
The officer told the driver to pull over and step out of the truck.
At the last stop the children climbed off the train with their bags.
The cyclist hopped off her bike and pushed it up the steep hill.
quiet: When the bus reached the market, we stayed on until the next stop.
The rider mounted her horse and crossed the stream at a trot.
If your tire goes flat, keep calm and slowly reduce your speed.
He climbed into the cab and gave the driver the address.
Hikers can follow the trail past the second bridge to reach the lake.
The officer waved the driver through the checkpoint without stopping.
At the first stop the children boarded the train with their bags.
The cyclist rode her bike all the way up the steep hill.

notes: Card: peaks on dis'mounted', 'pull off the road', 'get off the trail', 'got out of the vehicle', 'pull over', 下'車'. Near misses keep the same travel scenes but the person gets on/in or keeps going.
